notable.summary: Verify the component matrix of the dust tensor and show that its vanishing divergence produces the continuity equation and the pressure-free Euler equation.
notable.why_notable: Completes the chapter's central interpretive argument for why T is called the energy-momentum tensor.

notable.summary: Fill in the trace step taking the linearized field equations to their trace-reversed, slow-motion Poisson form and extract the 00 equation.
notable.why_notable: The only step in the kappa derivation the text skips; it is where the factor one half that produces 8 pi appears.

notable.summary: Show that the perfect-fluid conservation equations reduce to continuity and the Euler equation in Minkowski coordinates.
notable.why_notable: Supplies the omitted justification for lambda = 1 and mu = -1 and exposes where pressure enters relativistic inertia.

notable.summary: Use the tensor transformation of F^ab and j^a to find how E, B, charge density and current transform under an x-boost.
notable.why_notable: Turns the 'working hypothesis' of section 12.5 into testable predictions (e.g. a moving charge produces a magnetic field).

notable.summary: Reduce Maxwell's equations to sourced wave equations in a suitable gauge, identify the remaining gauge freedom, and deduce wave equations for E and B in empty regions.
notable.why_notable: Connects the covariant formalism to light as an electromagnetic wave.

notable.summary: Check that covariant and partial derivatives agree in the antisymmetrized field equations and in the potential relation.
notable.why_notable: A quick, reusable lemma: exterior-derivative-type equations are insensitive to the (symmetric) connection.

notable.summary: Carry out the metric variation that gives the Maxwell energy-momentum tensor, verify its energy and momentum densities, and show its conservation follows from Maxwell's equations.
notable.why_notable: The hardest computation of the chapter and the model for extracting T_ab from any matter Lagrangian.

notable.summary: Study the conservation equations of the energy-momentum tensor obtained from the massive scalar-field Lagrangian.
notable.why_notable: Shows that conservation of T_ab reproduces the field equation of the matter field itself, an open-ended exercise with little guidance.

difficulty.notes: Mathematically dense for its length: index gymnastics with Minkowski components, trace reversal in the linearized equations, first-order and metric variations of Lagrangians, and an eigenvalue problem with a Lorentzian metric. Conceptually it is mostly consolidation (conservation laws, Maxwell theory in tensor form) with two genuinely new ideas, the metric definition of T_ab and energy conditions. Novices struggle because many key steps are '(exercise)', a crucial ingredient is borrowed from Chapter 21, notation is overloaded (rho, phi, mu, T, u), units switch between Heaviside-Lorentz and Gaussian conventions, and some claims in section 12.9 are stated more strongly than they hold.

teaching_gems.gem: Explain T^00 = gamma^2 rho_0 as the product of two separate relativistic effects: more energy per particle and fewer cubic metres per particle.
teaching_gems.why_effective: It turns an abstract tensor component into a counting argument that learners can check, and shows immediately why density cannot be a scalar.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Boost a box of dust with a rapidity slider; two gauges (energy per particle, particle count per box) multiply into a T^00 bar, and a 4x4 heatmap of T^ab lights up its off-diagonal entries as speed grows.

teaching_gems.gem: Read the rows of the 4x4 dust matrix as conservation laws: row 0 is continuity, rows 1-3 are the momentum equation, which is where the name energy-momentum tensor comes from.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Gives a concrete, component-level meaning to the compact statement partial_b T^ab = 0 and ties it to fluid dynamics learners already know.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Clickable matrix: selecting a row highlights the corresponding flux arrows through the faces of a small spacetime cube and writes out the classical equation it becomes.

teaching_gems.gem: Fix kappa by demanding that weak-field, slow dust reproduce Poisson's equation; trace reversal and the 2 phi/c^2 in g_00 together produce the 8 pi.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Shows that the constant in Einstein's equations is not arbitrary and makes the correspondence principle an actual calculation.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Step-through derivation card deck where each step has a 'what if' toggle (skip trace reversal, forget the factor 2 in g_00) that shows the wrong kappa that would result.

teaching_gems.gem: Scarcity ansatz: list the only tensors a fluid can provide (u^a u^b and g^ab), write the most general combination, and let classical limits fix the coefficients.
teaching_gems.why_effective: A reusable recipe for building relativistic models, teaching learners to think about what structures are available rather than memorizing formulas.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Tensor builder: learner picks coefficients lambda and mu with sliders; the app shows the rest-frame matrix and the low-speed conservation equations, turning green when they match continuity and Euler.

teaching_gems.gem: Pause after the tensor rewriting of Maxwell's equations to say that indices alone prove nothing: the tensor transformation law is a hypothesis tested by experiment.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Models scientific honesty about the logical status of a formalism and prevents the common belief that notation guarantees covariance.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Boost a static charge: panel compares E and B predicted by transforming F^ab with the field computed directly from a moving-charge simulation, confirming the hypothesis visually.

teaching_gems.gem: First-order Lagrangian with phi_a and F_ab independent: the relation F = d phi and the antisymmetry of F come out of the variation instead of being put in.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Demonstrates the power of variational principles to generate structure, and echoes the Palatini idea from the previous chapter.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Interactive variational calculator: learner chooses which field to vary; the app highlights the terms that contribute and displays the resulting field equation.

teaching_gems.gem: Energy-momentum from how a Lagrangian responds to a change of metric: varying g^ab in the Maxwell action yields energy density (E^2 + B^2)/8 pi and the Poynting vector.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Connects abstract geometry (metric variation) to familiar electromagnetic energy and momentum, giving a universal definition of T_ab.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Field-configuration sandbox: learner sets E and B vectors; T_ab components, the energy density and a Poynting arrow update, with a toggle comparing covariant and contravariant components.

teaching_gems.gem: Use the eigenframe of T_a^b to describe any ordinary matter as a medium at rest with an energy density and three principal stresses; dust and perfect fluid become special cases, and the dominant energy condition becomes a simple inequality.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Unifies the chapter's models under one invariant picture and links to engineering stress intuition.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Stress ellipsoid viewer: learner sets mu and p_1, p_2, p_3; a 3D ellipsoid shows the stresses, a label names the matter type (dust, perfect fluid, anisotropic), and a warning appears if the dominant energy condition fails.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: The component form of the a = 0 conservation equation on p. 205 is printed without '= 0'.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: A careful reader may think it is an expression rather than an equation or wonder if something is missing.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Write the full equation with = 0 and immediately identify it with (12.8).

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: Equation (12.10) is called the Navier-Stokes equation, but without viscosity it is the Euler equation.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Confuses terminology and may lead learners to believe viscosity is included in the perfect fluid.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Name it Euler's equation and mention that Navier-Stokes adds viscous terms, which a perfect fluid lacks.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: The gamma^2 argument relies on 'relativistic mass', a concept many modern courses avoid.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Learners taught with invariant mass may reject or misinterpret the explanation.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Rephrase as energy per particle gamma m c^2 times number density gamma n.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: The linearized Einstein tensor and its gauge condition are imported from Chapter 21 without derivation.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: The kappa derivation rests on an unexplained formula; learners cannot verify it at this point.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Either give a short derivation of the linearized Ricci tensor or present a heuristic argument; flag clearly that this is a forward borrowing.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: The approximation 'neglect terms of order v/c and rho_0 v/c' is stated obscurely; the actual requirements (T^{0i}/T^{00} ~ v/c, T^{ij}/T^{00} ~ v^2/c^2, time derivatives negligible, phi/c^2 small) are not spelled out.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Unclear which approximations are needed and why only T_00 survives.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: List the orders of magnitude of each component and the role of each approximation.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: The claim that classical limits fix lambda = 1 is incomplete: pressure contributions to inertia are relativistic corrections invisible in the Newtonian limit; lambda + mu = 0 really follows from requiring rest-frame energy density rho_0.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Learners attempting Exercise 12.3 may find lambda undetermined and feel they erred.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: State the rest-frame requirement T^00 = rho_0 explicitly and treat mu = -1 as fixed by the pressure-gradient term.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: rho_0 in the perfect-fluid tensor is not distinguished from rest-mass density, and the equation of state switches to rho and uses T for temperature.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Notation clashes cause confusion between energy density, mass density, trace of T and temperature.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Use distinct symbols (e.g. rho for energy density, n or rho_m for rest-mass density, Theta for temperature) and explain internal energy.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: Units are inconsistent: section 12.5 declares Heaviside-Lorentz units (no 4 pi in Maxwell's equations), but (12.50), (12.57) and (12.59) use Gaussian 1/8 pi and 1/4 pi normalizations.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Learners checking factors against electrodynamics texts get mismatches of 4 pi.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Either use Gaussian units throughout (div E = 4 pi rho) or drop the 4 pi factors in the Lagrangian and T_ab; state the choice clearly.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: The index order F_ab = partial_b phi_a - partial_a phi_b and the overall sign of the matter Lagrangians differ from the most common conventions without comment.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Comparing with other books leads to sign errors and doubt about the results.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Add a conventions box comparing with Jackson or Carroll, and show that physical results (energy density positive) are unaffected.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: The gauge is called 'Lorentz gauge'; it is named after Ludvig Lorenz.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Minor historical inaccuracy, and a search for 'Lorenz gauge' in modern literature may be missed.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Use 'Lorenz gauge' with a note on the historical misattribution.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: The metric variation (12.55) is left entirely as an exercise, including the variation of sqrt(-g).
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: The central computation of section 12.7 is not demonstrated; many learners get stuck on delta sqrt(-g).
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Show the product-rule step and the formula delta sqrt(-g) = -(1/2) sqrt(-g) g_ab delta g^ab explicitly.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: Charged dust (12.62) is presented as a plain sum without showing how the conservation law yields the Lorentz force, despite the preceding remark that interacting fields need care.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Learners may think interactions are ignored or be puzzled by the apparent contradiction.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Show that nabla_b T^ab_EM = -F^a_b j^b (sign convention dependent) and hence rho_0 u^b nabla_b u^a equals the Lorentz force density.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: Section 12.9 says standard matter always yields real non-zero eigenvalues and a timelike eigenvector. But dust has zero principal stresses (zero eigenvalues), and null radiation such as a plane electromagnetic wave has no timelike eigenvector. Also, in signature (+,-,-,-) the eigenvalues of the mixed tensor T_a^b on the spacelike eigenvectors are -p_alpha, while the covariant frame components T_ij carry +p_alpha.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Learners may misapply the classification to null fields or be confused by sign errors in eigenvalues.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Introduce Hawking-Ellis types I and II, note the null exception, and distinguish eigenvalues of T_a^b from frame components T_ij.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: The statement that the dominant energy condition is equivalent to sound speed not exceeding light speed is imprecise; the DEC bounds p/rho, while sound speed depends on dp/d rho.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Leads to incorrect conclusions about causality of equations of state.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Say the DEC ensures energy flux is causal (non-spacelike) for all observers, and treat sound speed as a separate condition.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: The book asserts without qualification that every known matter field obeys the dominant energy condition. This is dated: quantum effects (Casimir energy) violate energy conditions, a cosmological constant sits on the boundary, and phantom dark-energy models violate it.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Gives an outdated view of the status of energy conditions in modern physics.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Present energy conditions as classical assumptions and mention known exceptions.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: The chapter calls nabla_b T^ab = 0 a conservation law in GR without cautioning that it does not imply global energy conservation.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Learners may believe total matter energy is conserved in expanding universes or dynamic spacetimes.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Explain the difference between local covariant conservation and integral conservation, which requires a Killing vector.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: Section 12.2 describes (12.1) as the 'simplest' second-rank tensor built from u^a and rho_0 and then says it turns out to be the energy-momentum tensor, but the only justification given is that its divergence reproduces the SR fluid equations; the alternative rho_0 g^ab (also built from available objects) is not discussed.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Learners may think the tensor is uniquely forced by simplicity rather than selected by matching conservation laws.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Ask the learner why rho_0 g^ab fails (its divergence gives grad rho_0 = 0, not fluid flow) before revealing that rho_0 u^a u^b works.

tutor_notes: Opening question: 'If a cloud of dust rushes past you at 60% of light speed, is it denser, less dense, or the same as for someone riding along with it?' Let the learner reason about mass and length contraction before revealing gamma^2.
For learners with fluids background, begin with the classical continuity and Euler equations and ask how to package density, momentum density and momentum flux into one object; then reveal T^ab.

Order for a first pass: dust tensor and its interpretation -> conservation law as fluid equations -> perfect fluid -> kappa from the Newtonian limit -> Maxwell tensor. The coupling-constant calculation can be postponed until the learner has seen linearized gravity.
Check for understanding: ask the learner to write T^ab for a perfect fluid at rest and to explain why the spatial diagonal entries are +p despite the minus sign in front of p g^ab (signature +---).
When deriving kappa, pause at the trace step and ask why T_00 - (1/2) T equals half of T_00 for dust; many learners miss that the trace equals T_00.
Common question: 'Why 8 pi and not 4 pi?' Answer with the two factors of 2: g_00 carries 2 phi/c^2, and trace reversal halves the effective source.
For Maxwell theory, have the learner fill in F^ab from E and B and verify one source equation (e.g. a = 0 gives Gauss's law) before trusting the compact form.
Emphasize the book's warning that index notation alone does not guarantee tensor behaviour; ask 'What experiment would test whether E and B mix under boosts as F^ab predicts?'
On gauge freedom, ask the learner to show that adding the gradient of any psi leaves F unchanged, then ask what extra condition Lorenz gauge places on psi.
Flag the units mismatch (Heaviside-Lorentz vs Gaussian) proactively when learners compare T_00 with their electromagnetism course.
When covering metric variation, write delta sqrt(-g) = -(1/2) sqrt(-g) g_ab delta g^ab on the board before starting; it is the most common sticking point.
Common question: 'Why do the covariant momentum components have a minus sign?' Explain index lowering in signature (+,-,-,-).
For section 12.9, draw an analogy with principal stresses in solid mechanics, then note where the analogy fails (null radiation has no rest frame).
Check for understanding of energy conditions: give example equations of state (p = rho/3 radiation, p = -rho vacuum energy, p = 2 rho) and ask which satisfy the dominant energy condition.
Address the misconception that nabla_b T^ab = 0 is global energy conservation, especially for learners headed to cosmology.

For section 12.8, have the learner compute nabla_b of the Maxwell part of the charged-dust tensor using Maxwell's equations with a source, so they see the Lorentz force appear; the book only asserts that the conservation equations give energy conservation and equations of motion.

residual_concerns: The dossier's tensor and sign checks (T_00, T_0alpha, (12.55), (12.57), perfect-fluid rest frame, kappa derivation, Klein-Gordon energy density sign) were redone by hand and agree with the book; the book's own unit mix (Heaviside-Lorentz Maxwell equations with Gaussian 1/4 pi normalization of T_ab) remains a genuine inconsistency in the source and is recorded as a gap.
